rationale: C15 is a clear material drafting template for the child. It regulates the same commodity, uses the same section 22 findings and representative period, and supplies the child's central quota machinery: a 26,000,000-pound aggregate limit, a 6,500,000-pound first-quarter sublimit, and identical country allocations for Argentina, Paraguay, and other countries. The child extends those quotas to three later annual periods and incorporates tung nuts through oil-equivalent calculations and direct-shipment rules closely associated with C06. C09 is a weaker structural analogue because it likewise combines aggregate periodic quotas with country allocations, but it concerns different products and lacks the distinctive numerical identity found in C15.

shared_material.child_excerpt: For each of the three twelve-month periods beginning on November 1, 1960, November 1, 1961, and November 1, 1962, the total aggregate quantity of tung oil and tung nuts (in terms of their oil equivalent) ... shall not exceed 26,000,000 pounds, of which not more than 6,500,000 pounds shall be entered or withdrawn during the first quarter
shared_material.parent_excerpt: for the 12 month period commencing November 1, 1958 ... [and] November 1, 1959 ... the total quantity of tung oil entered shall not exceed 26,000,000 pounds, of which no more than 6,500,000 pounds shall be entered during the first quarter
shared_material.explanation: The child carries forward C15's distinctive total and quarterly quota figures while extending the periods and combining tung oil with tung nuts on an oil-equivalent basis.

shared_material.child_excerpt: not more than 22,100,000 pounds shall be the product of Argentina, nor more than 2,964,000 pounds shall be the product of Paraguay, nor more than 936,000 pounds shall be the product of other foreign countries
shared_material.parent_excerpt: not more than 22,100,000 pounds shall be the product of Argentina, nor more than 2,964,000 pounds shall be the product of Paraguay, nor more than 936,000 pounds shall be the product of other foreign countries
shared_material.explanation: The country allocations are reproduced verbatim and constitute concrete, distinctive administrative machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: For the purposes of this proclamation the oil equivalent of tung nuts shall be computed on the basis of 15.9 pounds of oil for each 100 pounds of whole nuts, and on the basis of 35.8 pounds of oil for each 100 pounds of decorticated nuts.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: For the purposes of this proclamation the oil content of tung nuts shall be computed on the basis of 15.9 pounds for each 100 pounds of whole nuts, and on the basis of 35.8 pounds of oil for each 100 pounds of decorticated nuts.
shared_material.explanation: This language from C06 is essentially reproduced to integrate tung nuts into the oil-based quota inherited from C15.

shared_material.child_excerpt: all tung oil and tung nuts entered or withdrawn pursuant to this proclamation shall have been a direct shipment destined to the United States on an original through bill of lading from the country of production
shared_material.parent_excerpt: all tung oil and tung nuts entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption pursuant to the proclamation of September 9, 1957, or this proclamation, shall have been a direct shipment destined to the United States on an original through bill of lading from the country of production
shared_material.explanation: The child also reuses C06's distinctive direct-shipment requirement nearly verbatim.
